title: The stranger in white
hookLine: Jibril, unknown, asks about Islam, iman, ihsan and the Hour
carry: he came to teach you your religion
tomorrow: if Islam is a building, what's holding it up?

cards: A good teacher sometimes asks a question she already knows the answer to. So, what's seven times eight? Not to find out.
To get it said out loud, in front of everyone. Keep that in your pocket. Umar, yesterday's narrator, describes a day sitting with the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, when a man walks in.

His clothes are extremely white, his hair extremely black. There's no sign of travel on him, and none of them knows who he is. Two things that can't both be true: he's come from somewhere, and he's come from nowhere.
He sits down close, knee to knee with the Prophet, and starts asking.

teach.b: What is Islam? To testify there is no god but Allah and Muhammad is His messenger, to pray, to give zakat, to fast Ramadan, and to make the pilgrimage if you're able. What is iman, faith?

To believe in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, the Last Day, and the decree, its good and its bad. What is ihsan, excellence? To worship Allah as though you see Him, and if you don't see Him, He sees you.
And the Hour, when is it? The one asked knows no more about it than the one asking. Now the strange part.
After the answers, the stranger says: you've spoken truly.
Umar says they were amazed: he asks, and then he confirms. Who does that? Someone who already knows.
A while later the Prophet asks Umar if he knows who the questioner was, and then tells him: it was Jibril, who came to teach you your religion. So the questions were never for the asker.
They were for the people sitting in the circle, who heard the whole religion laid out in three rings: what you do, what you believe, and how you stand before Allah while you do it.

teach.h: HE CAME TO TEACH YOU YOUR RELIGION.

how: Teachers use the hadith of Jibril as an outline of the faith in three parts, Islam, iman and ihsan, and students learn its questions and answers, often in Arabic as well.

games.q: what does “the stranger in white” mean?
o: a traveler who came to test the Prophet
Jibril, who came unknown to teach by asking
an unknown companion who asked about prayer

games.q: the stranger's questions — tap the pairs.
p: believe: Allah, angels, books, the Last Day
worship as though you see Him
the one asked knows no more

s: Jibril asked because he didn't know the answers
he said 'you've spoken truly' after the answers. the questions were for the people listening.
the stranger showed no sign of travel, yet nobody knew him
that's the puzzle Umar notices: from somewhere, yet from nowhere.
in this hadith, ihsan means being kind to people
here it's worshipping Allah as though you see Him, and knowing He sees you.

games.q: your little cousin is learning the steps of prayer, and you're fairly sure she knows them. how do you help them stick?
o: ask her to walk you through them, and tell her each time she's right.
recite all the steps for her again, slowly, so nothing gets missed.
skip it: if she already knows them, there's nothing left to teach.
games.why: Jibril taught by asking and confirming: 'you've spoken truly.' the questions put the answers out loud, where everyone could hear them.

practice: Sit the way a student sits close to a teacher: upright, knees settled, hands resting on your thighs.

Go back through the three answers slowly in your mind, one at a time: what you do, what you believe, and worship as though you see Him. Stay with that last one, and the line after it, for the rest of the sit.

wordCard.voice: The stranger in white: Jibril, the angel Gabriel, who came as a questioner. His questions became the three words of the hadith: Islam, iman, ihsan.

orig.note: Arabic: Gabriel, the angel. in this hadith he arrives as an unknown questioner.

carryVoice: Pocket this one: he came to teach you your religion, by asking and not by lecturing. See you tomorrow.

sources.ref: Sahih Muslim 8 (Umar: the stranger in white; Islam, iman, ihsan, the Hour; 'it was Jibril')
